lines.raw: Patient or member?
lines.say: Patient or member?

lines.raw: A **patient** is anyone who receives care.
lines.say: A patient is anyone who receives care.

lines.raw: When that person has health insurance, the insurance company calls them a **member** of its plan.
lines.say: When that person has health insurance, the insurance company calls them a member of its plan.

lines.raw: Emily is Dr. Patel's **patient**, and she is a **member** of her employer's plan.
lines.say: Emily is Doctor Patel's patient, and she is a member of her employer's plan.

lines.raw: Same person, two names, depending on who is talking.

lines.raw: Member.

lines.raw: A person covered by a health plan.
lines.say: A person covered by a health plan.

lines.raw: Each member has a **member ID**.
lines.say: Each member has a member I D.

lines.raw: Where do Americans get coverage?
lines.say: Where do Americans get coverage?

lines.raw: Every American falls into one (or sometimes more than one) of these groups.
lines.say: Every American falls into one (or sometimes more than one) of these groups.

lines.raw: The numbers are **approximate** and change a little each year.
lines.say: The numbers are approximate and change a little each year.

lines.raw: Main sources of US health coverage (approximate shares of the population).
lines.say: Main sources of U S health coverage (approximate shares of the population).

lines.raw: **Employer plan**. Who it is for: Workers and their families. Roughly how many: About **half** of Americans. Nepal comparison: Ram's startup group policy.
lines.say: Employer plan. Who it is for: Workers and their families. Roughly how many: About half of Americans. Nepal comparison: Ram's startup group policy.

lines.raw: **Medicare**. Who it is for: People **65 and older**, and some younger people with disabilities. Roughly how many: Close to **1 in 5**. Nepal comparison: A national scheme earned through years of work and tax, a bit like SSF.
lines.say: Medicare. Who it is for: People 65 and older, and some younger people with disabilities. Roughly how many: Close to 1 in 5. Nepal comparison: A national scheme earned through years of work and tax, a bit like S S F.

lines.raw: **Medicaid** (and **CHIP** for children). Who it is for: People with **low income**, run by each state. Roughly how many: Close to **1 in 5**. Nepal comparison: Government help for poor families.
lines.say: Medicaid (and CHIP for children). Who it is for: People with low income, run by each state. Roughly how many: Close to 1 in 5. Nepal comparison: Government help for poor families.

lines.raw: **Individual / Marketplace** (ACA). Who it is for: People who buy their own, e.g. self-employed. Roughly how many: Roughly **1 in 10**. Nepal comparison: Buying your own policy from an insurer.
lines.say: Individual or Marketplace (A C A). Who it is for: People who buy their own, for example self-employed. Roughly how many: Roughly 1 in 10. Nepal comparison: Buying your own policy from an insurer.

lines.raw: **Military** (TRICARE, VA). Who it is for: Soldiers, veterans and their families. Roughly how many: A few percent. Nepal comparison: Army and police hospitals for service families.
lines.say: Military (TRICARE, V A). Who it is for: Soldiers, veterans and their families. Roughly how many: A few percent. Nepal comparison: Army and police hospitals for service families.

lines.raw: **Uninsured**. Who it is for: People with no cover at all. Roughly how many: About **8%** (roughly 1 in 12). Nepal comparison: Paying everything out of pocket.
lines.say: Uninsured. Who it is for: People with no cover at all. Roughly how many: About 8 percent (roughly 1 in 12). Nepal comparison: Paying everything out of pocket.

lines.raw: Why the shares add up to more than 100%.
lines.say: Why the shares add up to more than 100 percent.

lines.raw: Some people have **two** sources at once.
lines.say: Some people have two sources at once.

lines.raw: For example, a low-income person over 65 can have both Medicare and Medicaid (called **dual eligible**), and some retirees have Medicare plus a plan from their old employer.
lines.say: For example, a low-income person over 65 can have both Medicare and Medicaid (called dual eligible), and some retirees have Medicare plus a plan from their old employer.

lines.raw: So if you add the shares, you get more than 100%.
lines.say: So if you add the shares, you get more than 100 percent.

lines.say: In the U S: Our U S family, labelled.

lines.say: She is the subscriber.

lines.say: Daniel (M 1 0 0 3): employer plan as Emily's dependent, from 1 July 2025.

lines.say: Before he lost his job, he had cover through his own employer.

lines.raw: **Lily** (`M1002`): **employer plan** as Emily's dependent.
lines.say: Lily (M 1 0 0 2): employer plan as Emily's dependent.

lines.raw: **Robert** (Emily's father): **Medicare**, because he is over 65.
lines.say: Robert (Emily's father): Medicare, because he is over 65.

lines.raw: From 2022 to 2023 he had **Original Medicare** (run directly by the government) plus a separate **Part D** plan for medicines.
lines.say: From 2022 to 2023 he had Original Medicare (run directly by the government) plus a separate Part D plan for medicines.

lines.raw: What does being uninsured mean?
lines.say: What does being uninsured mean?

lines.raw: An uninsured person can still get care, but must pay the full bill, often at a higher price than an insurer would pay.
lines.say: An uninsured person can still get care, but must pay the full bill, often at a higher price than an insurer would pay.

lines.raw: US hospital **emergency departments** must check and stabilise anyone with an emergency, whether or not they can pay.
lines.say: U S hospital emergency departments must check and stabilise anyone with an emergency, whether or not they can pay.

lines.raw: But the bill still comes later.
lines.say: But the bill still comes later.

lines.raw: Like most patients in Nepal.
lines.say: Like most patients in Nepal.

lines.raw: An uninsured American is in the same position as a Nepali family with no SSF, no Health Insurance Board cover and no private policy: every ticket, test and medicine is paid at the counter.
lines.say: An uninsured American is in the same position as a Nepali family with no S S F, no Health Insurance Board cover and no private policy: every ticket, test and medicine is paid at the counter.

lines.raw: The difference is the size of the bill.
lines.say: The difference is the size of the bill.

lines.raw: A US hospital stay can cost more than a Nepali family earns in years.
lines.say: A U S hospital stay can cost more than a Nepali family earns in years.

lines.raw: What a member pays.
lines.say: What a member pays.

lines.raw: Having insurance does not mean care is free.
lines.say: Having insurance does not mean care is free.

lines.raw: A member pays a regular **premium** just to have cover, and a share of the bill (such as a fixed **copay**) when they use care.
lines.say: A member pays a regular premium just to have cover, and a share of the bill (such as a fixed copay) when they use care.

lines.raw: For example, Emily's strep throat visit on **10 March 2025** had a plan-agreed price of **$102**: she paid a **$25 copay** and the plan paid the other **$77**.
lines.say: For example, Emily's strep throat visit on 10 March 2025 had a plan-agreed price of 102 dollars: she paid a 25 dollars copay and the plan paid the other 77 dollars.
